Most Albertans don't want to leave Canada. So why are separatist organizers asking Donald Trump's government for help?

Danielle Smith says she wants Alberta to stay in Canada. Her government has also helped open a route towards another independence referendum. Some voters want to send Ottawa a message. The organizers campaigning for independence have a timetable for building a country. Those are very different expectations to bring to the same ballot.

To understand how we got here, we're following Alberta's fight over land, oil, and political power: the resource arrangements imposed when the province was created, the National Energy Program, Stephen Harper's firewall letter, equalization, and the pipelines Ottawa has spent billions supporting. Who gets the oil money, and why does an industry with this much government support keep presenting itself as shut out?

Then we follow the people selling separation. An inauthentic YouTube network uses hired presenters, AI voices, and invented claims to make a minority movement look much bigger. Some operators are chasing advertising revenue. Separately, American officials have taken meetings with separatists while denying that they made any commitments. We look at what the evidence establishes, and what an independent, landlocked Alberta would
